newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Maruti to recall 50,000 cars.
newsitem.headline: India's Maruti to recall 50,000 cars.

text.p: India's largest carmaker Maruti Udyog Ltd said on Saturday it planned to recall 50,000 cars sold between November 1996 and April 1997 after finding defective steering systems were installed in about 1,500 of them.

"This defective part has gone into a very small percentage of cars and we are recalling 50,000 cars made during a certain period," Maruti spokesman Arun Arora told Reuters. "About 1,500 cars are expected to be defective."
He said the company would place an advertisement in Indian newspapers that would identify the cars by their chassis and engine numbers, and ask consumers to bring the vehicles back to the factory.
"Then we will check them. Whichever has a defective part, we will replace it free of cost," Arora said. "The estimate of the cost to us is still being worked out."
Each defective component, a pinion in the steering assembly, costs about 100 rupees ($2.80), Arora said.
He said the defect was a metallurgical fault that originated in steering system components manufactured by India's Mukund Steel and supplied to Maruti by Sona Steering SyStems Ltd .
"This defect is not hazardous," Arora added. "There is no safety risk, but we are recalling the cars because there is a slight deviation from our specifications."

The Economic Times quoted Sona managing director Surinder Kapoor as saying: "Our tests show that the components would not prove hazardous but they need to be changed as they are not made to the desired specifications."
Maruti is a 50-50 joint venture between the Indian government and Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp. It sold 338,690 vehicles in 1996/97 (April-March).
Its 800-cc hatchback model, in which the defective steering systems are installed, commands more than 80 percent of the small car segment of India's automobile market.
The company's profit after tax rose to 5.01 billion rupees in 1996/97 from 4.28 billion in the previous year, riding a 23 percent surge in sales. (1=35.8 rupees)
